chunks: Abān narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Whatever the snare catches and severs from it, then it is carrion. And whatever you reach from the rest of its body alive, then slaughter it properly; thereafter eat from it.”

key_terms.الْحِبَالَةُ: a snare or trap used in hunting
key_terms.حَيّاً: alive at the time it is found
key_terms.فَذَكِّهِ: perform proper slaughter on it according to the shar'i method
key_terms.قَطَعَتْ: severed or cut off from the animal
key_terms.كُلْ: eat from it after valid slaughter
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: carrion; an animal unlawfully dead and not halal to eat

ai.seo_question: If a trapped animal is partially severed by a snare, which part is halal to eat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding hunted animals caught in a snare. Any part severed by the snare is treated as carrion, while the remaining body may only be eaten if it is found alive and then properly slaughtered.
